## Summary

Fixes #45.

The look from the issue's JSON is now the default and is offered as the **Matrix universe** preset. The previous defaults are kept as **Glass universe**, so nothing is lost.

The custom frame (the shape, size and width of each corner and side) is now drawn on every bordered element: outer panels, panels inside panels, list blocks, buttons, fields, chips, tags, selects and menus. Inner blocks and controls use smaller corners.

The full case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-45/README.md`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-45-bac51f6e4d8d/docs/case-studies/issue-45/README.md). It includes the requirements table, research on existing libraries (Arwes, augmented-ui) and platform features (CSS `corner-shape`, `border-image`, `overflow: clip`, `::selection`), the sources of the palette colours, the glitches found and their root causes, and the validation.

### Requirements → changes

| # | Requirement | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | The JSON is the default look, offered as the "Matrix universe" preset | `src/settings/schema.defaults.js` and `src/settings/presets.js` add Matrix universe (the new defaults) and Glass universe (the old defaults) |
| R2 | Outer panels, inner blocks, buttons and other bordered elements share the per-side and per-corner frame | `src/skins.frames.js` adds `PANELS`, `BLOCKS` and `CONTROLS` with corner scales `corner.blockScale` (0.6) and `corner.controlScale` (0.35). New settings `corner.blocks` (frame / line) and `corner.controls` (frame / border) bring back the old look |
| R3 | Content that does not fit is cut | `ui.overflow` (clip by default / visible) puts `overflow: clip` on panels, plus the frame's `clip-path` |
| R4 | Transparent backgrounds and selection | `ui.selection` (accent / accent2 / system) and `ui.selectionOpacity`. The colour chooser and the menu stay readable on a fully transparent surface |
| R5 | Width of the top highlight | `future.accentWidth`, `future.accentMax` and `future.accentStyle` (solid / center / glow). The stat strip now uses its size as its height |
| R6 | Separate widths for corners and sides | `corner.{tl,tr,br,bl}Width`, `corner.{top,right,bottom,left}Width` and `corner.edgeStyle` (solid / dashed / dotted). "Make all corners like this one" also copies the width |
| R7 | A corner layer, on top by default, that covers the left colour bar of positions | `corner.layer` (top / below). On top, the frame is drawn by a `::after` overlay with `pointer-events: none` |
| R8 | More configuration and a better-looking preset | 20 new settings in total, and 7 glitches fixed (see the case study, section 4) |
| R9 | Small samples of every UI element, to find glitches | `src/pages/UiSamples.jsx` on the settings page: panel, inner block, position, stat, overflow, buttons, fields, select, colour, textarea, chips, tags, segmented control, tabs, table |
| R10 | Neon and pastel palettes, not only sliders | `src/components/colorPalettes.js` adds Neon (10), Pastel (10) and Matrix (8) colours to every colour chooser. Every neon and pastel value comes from a named colour list, with its source noted |
| R11 | A deep case study with research | `docs/case-studies/issue-45/` (README, data, before and after screenshots) |

### Glitches found with the samples (each has a test that failed before the fix)

1. Inside framed panels, controls had square dashed boxes. They now get the frame with smaller corners.
2. Colour swatches were painted over by the control background. The swatch is now a child element.
3. The stat accent strip ignored its size, because the size went to `width`. It now sets `height`.
4. Selected text was system blue on the green look. The new `ui.selection` setting fixes this.
5. The left colour bar of a position ran through the cut corner. The new `corner.layer` setting fixes this.
6. The samples of outer panels looked like inner blocks because they sit inside a settings panel. A `[data-frame-root]` element now starts a new nesting level for the frame.
7. Long content spilled over the frame. `ui.overflow` fixes this.

**Other looks of the samples**:

## Tests

- **Unit tests** (Vitest)
  - `src/skins.issue-45.test.jsx` (14 tests): the frame on panels, blocks and controls; the corner scales; the outer samples staying outer; the side, corner and accent widths; the corner layer; overflow; selection; and "make all corners like this one".
  - `src/components/ColorInput.test.jsx`: the palettes, and that every colour is a valid, unique hex value.
  - `src/pages/issue-45.test.jsx`: the samples.
  - `src/settings/settings.test.js`, `src/settings/presets.test.js`: the defaults and the presets.
  - The existing applied-settings tests check that every new choice has a CSS rule.
  - `src/skins.frames.restyle.test.js` (6 tests): the shapes and lines of the corners sit on the root only, every framed element is its own selector, the points and line layers match the old ones, and no long formula of the frame is inherited (the root computes typed `@property` lengths). It fails on the commits before the WebKit fix.
  - `src/workflow.test.js`: a job that takes its timeout from the matrix must have a timeout in every matrix entry.
- **Browser check in CI**: `npm run test:ui:issue45` (`experiments/issue-45-browser.mjs`) is a new step in the Chromium, Firefox and WebKit browser matrix. It makes 16 checks:
  - the corner scales: 1 for outer panels, 0.6 for inner blocks, 0.35 for controls;
  - the frame cuts a panel, an inner block, a button and a field;
  - overflow is clipped;
  - the chooser stays in view, shows the three palettes, and "Neon pink" sets `#ff10f0`;
  - with `corner.blocks: line` and `corner.controls: border`, only the outer panels keep the frame;
  - with the layer on top, the frame overlays the position;
  - switching the corner layer moves no positioned element;
  - no page errors occur.

  It passes locally in all three engines.
- **Issue #39 browser checks**: `experiments/issue-39-browser.mjs` and `experiments/issue-39-visual-review.mjs` asserted the old Glass universe defaults, so with the new default they failed in CI (`issue-39-browser.mjs:95` expected `glass`, and the visual review found 14 defects). They now start from the Glass universe look they were written for. That look is computed from `PREVIOUS_DEFAULTS` in `src/settings/schema.js`.
- **Experiments** used for the screenshots and glitch hunting: `experiments/issue-45-samples.mjs`, `issue-45-zoom.mjs`, `issue-45-picker.mjs`, `issue-45-positions.mjs` (the corner layer moves nothing on 11 pages) and `issue-45-computed.mjs`.

### The WebKit CI job and its time limit

With the Matrix universe as the default, the `network-browsers (webkit, macos-15-intel)` job first ran out of its 15 minutes. On `main` it already took 11 min 55 s. The full analysis is in section 7 of [the case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-45-bac51f6e4d8d/docs/case-studies/issue-45/README.md).

- **Root cause.** Every framed element declared 49 custom properties of its own (`calc()` of `var()`, a 36-point polygon, and the sizes and positions of 20 layers). WebKit compares every inherited custom property of every element when `<html>` restyles, which the issue #27 audit does on each slider key press.
- **Fix.** The root computes the lengths of each scale once as typed `@property` lengths. Framed elements draw from them in properties that do not inherit (`src/skins.frames.properties.css`).
- **Measured.** `experiments/issue-45-webkit-diagnose.mjs` ran as a temporary CI step. One restyle of `/settings/` in WebKit dropped from 1680 ms to 378 ms. For comparison, the same Matrix look on `main` takes 272 ms and the Glass look on `main` 107 ms.
- **Tried and dropped.** Each of these was timed with `experiments/issue-45-ab-sheets.mjs`, which alternates sheet sets A, B, A, B so machine load slows both alike. None helped beyond the noise:
  - unitless numbers per element instead of root lengths (390 ms against 340 ms);
  - dropping `--fx-scale` (269 against 298 ms);
  - `content-visibility: auto` on the off-screen settings groups (WebKit still restyles them).

  `experiments/issue-45-inherited-count-micro.mjs` shows the floor that is left: 500 inherited root lengths cost about 26 ms on 1800 elements.
- **Time limits.** The job still does not fit in 15 minutes. The page has 111 sliders instead of 93, the default look restyles about 2.5 times slower than `main`'s Glass default, and issue #45 adds its own step. With a temporary 45-minute limit, the job measured 16 min 45 s (run 41243894083): the issue #27 step took 5 min instead of 1 min 53 s. On a busy runner (run 41246513747, every step 1.3 to 1.5 times slower) WebKit took 23 min 51 s, and Chromium hit its 15 minutes. In Chromium each settings slider costs the same as on `main`; the job is longer only because of the extra sliders and the new step. The browser matrix now sets the limit per engine:

  | Engine | `main` | branch | branch, busy runner | limit |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Chromium | 9 min 2 s | 11 min 7 s | over 15 min | 20 min |
  | Firefox | 5 min 48 s | 7 min 13 s | 8 min 29 s | 15 min |
  | WebKit (macOS) | 11 min 55 s | 16 min 45 s | 23 min 51 s | 30 min |

  With these limits every job passed in run 41249574127 (WebKit 21 min 54 s, Chromium 11 min 30 s, Firefox 8 min 48 s) and in run 41251904042 on the final commit (WebKit 22 min 0 s, Chromium 14 min 33 s, Firefox 9 min 7 s).

### How to reproduce

1. Run `npm ci && npm run dev`, open `/settings/`, and open **Samples of every element**.
2. Change the corner, frame, border, selection or overflow settings and watch the samples.
3. Pick **Matrix universe** or **Glass universe** under presets.
4. Click any colour swatch to see the palettes.
